title: Burst-Hedging and Soft-Preemption for Tiered Routing with Quota-Aware Prioritization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a robust admission and mitigation strategy that preserves enterprise and paid customer SLOs while allowing free-tier burst traffic to proceed in a controlled manner. This ticket designs and lands a 'burst-hedging' policy plus a soft-preemption path which rebalances requests across tiers and regions, falls back to cheaper model variants when necessary, and maintains quota fairness over rolling windows. Goal: reduce P50/P95 latency regression for paid/enterprise during cross-region demand spikes while minimizing failed requests for free-tier users.
proposed_solution: 1) Admission controller maintains per-tenant and per-tier credit buckets (time-decayed) and a short-term burst buffer. 2) On request arrival, perform hierarchical checks: tier quota -> region affinity -> model-variant compatibility. 3) If quota-exceeded for a higher tier, attempt soft-preemption: optionally demote request to lower-cost model variant OR route to a different region with spare capacity respecting data residency flags. 4) Implement hedging: send a parallel lightweight probe to alternative routing path when predicted latency > threshold, and take first complete response with deduplication. 5) Circuit-breaker and budget banking: allow small temporary overdraw for enterprise tenants with automatic reconciliation and throttling when debt exceeds threshold. 6) Expose per-tenant telemetry and debuggable decision logs for audit/QA.
acceptance_criteria: Paid + Enterprise P95 latency does not increase by more than 5% under 2x baseline free-tier burst for 30m in load test
Free-tier request failure rate under burst stays below 1% after hedging and demotion policies
Model-variant fallback produces no more than 3% semantic regression on representative eval prompt set (suites/run-variant-eval)
Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 and configurable via console: enable/disable, bank size, preempt thresholds
Automated infra tests: unit tests for admission controller, integration test for regional fallback and hedging behaviour
Observability: new dashboards surfaced in Console for credit balances, hedging rate, preemption events, and rollback kill-switch
rollout_plan: Day 0: Merge RFC + implementation behind feature flag (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287)
Canary week: 1% of traffic, only non-PHI tenants, monitor latency and preemption signals; manual rollback window 4h
Scale: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over successive days if metrics OK; enable enterprise bank reconciliation for pilot customers on 20% step
Failover: if paid P95 latency exceeds threshold for two consecutive 10m buckets, auto-disable hedging and demotion globally and notify SRE
Post-rollout: 72h stability watch followed by retro and tuning of thresholds and bank sizes
notes: 2026-03-01: Spike replay experiments ran using synthetic traces for three tenants. Observed 12% dropped tokens for paid tier under naive overdraw. Introduced banking reduced drops to 0.7% (Arjun).
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and Design. PM (Liam O'Connor) requested console toggles and per-tenant visible credit balance. Add console-2026.03 task in follow-up.

2026-03-06: Security asked about data residency when routing regions; added region affinity check and explicit opt-out for cross-region fallback (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/routing/ENG-99001-design).

2026-03-08: Load test 2x baseline showed hedging reduced tail latency by 18% for paid but increased overall token cost by ~4% for those requests. Decision: enable hedging for enterprise+paid only by default; allow free-tier opt-in via config.
2026-03-10: Implementation PR opened (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287). Requesting review from @sofia and @tj-sre for SRE/observability hooks.
2026-03-12: Partial rollout: feature flagged on staging. Integration tests failing intermittently for dedup logic; assigned to Arjun and QA to triage (see failing test logs in the PR).
